answer: Agent economies can resist sybils by anchoring every identity to a verified real-world vertex — a hardware key, a bank-verified account, or a registered org — so one machine spinning up ten thousand ghosts still yields just one vertex in the trust graph. Around each vertex grows a grove of earned history: completed jobs, counterparty endorsements, dispute records that take months to accumulate. Even a cheap copper-tier anchor forces attackers to buy distinct real-world roots for every fake battalion, and graph analysis prunes branches no honest agent endorsed. Sybils stop being free.
